messages:
Ashley: Quick question — for canary rollouts that span multiple regions + two model variants (int8 and fp16), what's our canonical fallback order when capacity gets tight?
Ravi: Are you thinking region failover first or model-variant fallback first?
Ashley: Yeah. We have two real customers wanting different defaults. One prefers staying in-region and degrading model precision; the other prefers keeping model quality and routing cross-region.
Matt: From runtime POV, cross-region adds latency + egress cost. My gut: prefer same-region variant fallback -> region failover as last resort.
Julia: +1 for region-first only if latency SLOs can tolerate it. We should default to "latency-first" vs "quality-first" policies.
Kevin: Is there an API change needed? rollouts currently accept traffic split and fallback list but semantics are vague.
Ashley: Thinking of a compact rolloutSpec field: 

```
rolloutSpec {
  traffic: {canary: 10, stable: 90}
  fallback_preference: ["variant","region"]
  fallback_hooks: {on_capacity: "soft-hedge", on_latency_spike: "failover"}
}
```

Would let Console show a dropdown with presets (latency-first, quality-first, cost-first).
Ravi: Runtime needs deterministic arbitration: if multiple fallbacks available, evaluate in order and run capacity check per candidate. Also attach telemetry tags for what triggered fallback.
Matt: Telemetry: include fields: fallback_reason, from_model, to_model, from_region, to_region, tokens_affected. We can then correlate with cost/regression alerts.
Julia: UX note: console should visualize expected p95 change if you pick a preset. We can simulate using historical traces.
Kevin: Concern: permissioning. Enterprise tenants might want to lock fallback ordering. Add a rollout lock flag that prevents Console overrides.
Ashley: OpsBot: deploy plan? OpsBot: @channel rollout plan created: rollout/2012-canary-42 queued. No changes to runtime API yet.
Matt: One more edge: quota enforcement. If canary exhausts per-tenant quota in region A, variant fallback will still fail if quota bound to tenant+region. So order needs to consider quota constraints first — maybe add a pre-check pass.
Ravi: Good point. Proposal: evaluation pipeline: 1) feasibility (quota/capacity) 2) policy-ordered fallback list 3) enforce. Feasibility can short-circuit.
Julia: That lets us keep simple ordering but ensures we won't try useless fallbacks.
Ashley: OK — I'll draft an RFC with rolloutSpec example, console presets, telemetry table, and runtime pre-check step. Can people review tomorrow?
Kevin: Review by EOD for me.
Matt: I'll sketch the runtime change in a PR and add telemetry fields.
Ravi: I'll add design for feasibility checks + enforcement.
Ashley: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Reminder: meeting tomorrow 11:30am to align on rollout UX and API.
